Container.Overview:
Dawarich is a self-hosted web app designed to replace Google Timeline (aka Google Location History). Visualize your data on an interactive map, import your location history from Google Maps Timeline and Owntracks, and explore statistics like the number of countries and cities visited, total distance traveled, and more!
This template is setting up the production version of the app. NOTE: Do not use autoupdate and do not update any Dawarich container without backing up your data first and checking for breaking changes in the updating guides. https://dawarich.app/docs/self-hosting/updating/ https://dawarich.app/docs/self-hosting/maintenance/backup-and-restore/

Container.Requires: For Dawarich production 3 docker containers are required: - dawarich_app - Dawarich web application including Sidekiq worker for background jobs - dawarich_db - PostGIS database - dawarich_redis - Redis database

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the Dawarich web interface (container port 3000).

Config.Name: Imports Path
Config.Description: Path to watch for imports

Config.Name: Storage Path
Config.Description: Path to store application data

Config.Name: Database Path
Config.Description: Path to store database data

Config.Name: Web Files Path
Config.Description: Path to web files

Config.Name: Secret Key Base
Config.Description: Signs sessions and cookies, and derives encryption keys that aren't set explicitly. Required in production. Generate a value with openssl rand -hex 64 and keep it: changing it signs everyone out and can make encrypted data unreadable.

Config.Name: Application Hosts
Config.Description: Application hosts, provide multiple if you want your Dawarich instance to be available by multiple domains/ip addresses. Don't put protocols here, only host names.

Config.Name: Application Protocol
Config.Description: Application protocol. Change to https if you want your Dawarich instance to be served via SSL

Config.Name: Domain
Config.Description: Public hostname used to build absolute URLs in outgoing emails (family invitations, digest emails, password resets). Required in production - leaving it unset will cause email delivery to fail with a URL generation error. No protocol, no trailing slash. Example: dawarich.example.com.

Config.Name: Time Zone
Config.Description: Time zone. Full list of supported timezones available on Github

Config.Name: Distance Unit
Config.Description: Distance unit. For miles, change to mi. All settings still should be provided in meters/kilometers

Config.Name: Min Minutes Spent In City
Config.Description: Minimum minutes spent in a city

Config.Name: Database Host
Config.Description: Database host

Config.Name: Database Username
Config.Description: Database username

Config.Name: Database Password
Config.Description: Database password

Config.Name: Database Name
Config.Description: Database name. An existing dawarich_development database remains usable when RAILS_ENV is production.

Config.Name: Database Port
Config.Description: Database port

Config.Name: Rails Max Threads
Config.Description: Connection pool size for the Dawarich database

Config.Name: Redis URL
Config.Description: Redis URL. Redis 8 is the default; Valkey also works

Config.Name: Rails Cache DB
Config.Description: Redis cache database

Config.Name: Rails Job Queue DB
Config.Description: Redis job queue database

Config.Name: Rails WS DB
Config.Description: Redis WebSocket database

Config.Name: Self Hosted
Config.Description: Set to true if you're self-hosting Dawarich

Config.Name: Rails ENV
Config.Description: Application environment. Self-hosted instances should use `production`. `development` is for working on Dawarich itself: it reloads code when it changes and logs every SQL query. See Switching an existing instance to production: https://dawarich.app/docs/self-hosting/environment-variables/#switching-an-existing-instance-to-production.

Config.Name: Sidekiq Embedded
Config.Description: Run background jobs inside the web process. Leave it unset when you run a separate worker.

Config.Name: Web Concurrency
Config.Description: Number of web worker processes. Keep 0 with embedded jobs.

Config.Name: Background Processing Concurrency
Config.Description: Background job threads. More info on Sidekiq docs

Config.Name: Sidekiq Username
Config.Description: Sidekiq dashboard username

Config.Name: Sidekiq Password
Config.Description: Sidekiq dashboard password

Config.Name: OIDC Client ID
Config.Description: OIDC client ID from your identity provider

Config.Name: Archive Raw Data
Config.Description: Enable archival of raw import data. When enabled, original import files are preserved for potential re-processing.

Config.Name: Archive Encryption Key
Config.Description: Encryption key for raw data archives. Required when ARCHIVE_RAW_DATA is true. Preserve the original key to keep existing archives readable.

Config.Name: Photon API Host
Config.Description: Photon API host. Useful if you're self-hosting your own Photon instance

Config.Name: Reverse Geocoding RPS
Config.Description: Requests per second your provider allows. Set it for Geoapify, LocationIQ or the public Nominatim. photon.komoot.io is always limited to 1.

Config.Name: Reverse Geocoding Concurrency
Config.Description: Reverse-geocoding threads across all workers. No limit when no rate is set. See Background jobs.

Config.Name: Photon API Key
Config.Description: Photon API key. Useful if you're supporting Dawarich development on Patreon and want to use Photon API instance hosted by Freika without any limits

Config.Name: Photon API Use HTTPS
Config.Description: Use HTTPS for Photon API requests. Set to true if you're using your own Photon instance behind a reverse proxy with SSL

Config.Name: Photon API Language
Config.Description: Language Dawarich asks Photon for place names in: a two-letter code such as nl, or default for names in the local language. Your Photon index must include it. Can also be set under Admin → Instance settings. See Photon index languages

Config.Name: Geoapify API Key
Config.Description: Geoapify API key. Provide your own key if you want to use Geoapify reverse geocoding service

Config.Name: Nominatim API Host
Config.Description: Nominatim API host. Useful if you're self-hosting your own Nominatim instance

Config.Name: Nominatim API Key
Config.Description: Nominatim API key. Provide your own key if you want to use Nominatim reverse geocoding service

Config.Name: Nominatim API Use HTTPS
Config.Description: Use HTTPS for Nominatim API requests. Set to true if you're using a Nominatim instance behind a reverse proxy with SSL

Config.Name: Store Geodata
Config.Description: Set to true if you want to store geodata in the database. This will increase the size of the database and will require more disk space.

Config.Name: Prometheus Exporter Enabled
Config.Description: Enable Prometheus metrics exporter

Config.Name: Metrics Username
Config.Description: HTTP basic auth username Prometheus uses to scrape /metrics. Required.

Config.Name: Metrics Password
Config.Description: HTTP basic auth password. Required.

Config.Name: OTP Encryption Primary Key
Config.Description: Primary key for encrypting OTP secrets. Set explicitly to enable two-factor authentication.

Config.Name: OTP Encryption Deterministic Key
Config.Description: Deterministic key for OTP encryption. Set explicitly to enable two-factor authentication.

Config.Name: OTP Encryption Key Derivation Salt
Config.Description: Salt for OTP key derivation. Set explicitly to enable two-factor authentication.

Config.Name: OIDC Client Secret
Config.Description: OIDC client secret from your identity provider

Config.Name: OIDC Issuer
Config.Description: OIDC issuer URL (enables auto-discovery)

Config.Name: OIDC Redirect URI
Config.Description: Callback URL. Defaults to {APPLICATION_URL}/users/auth/openid_connect/callback

Config.Name: OIDC Provider Name
Config.Description: Custom display name for the OIDC login button

Config.Name: OIDC Auto Register
Config.Description: Automatically create accounts for new OIDC users

Config.Name: OIDC PKCE Enabled
Config.Description: Enable PKCE (S256) for the authorization code flow. Required when your OIDC client enforces PKCE (e.g. Pocket ID, hardened Authentik/Keycloak)

Config.Name: Allow Email Password Registration
Config.Description: Allow traditional email/password registration alongside OIDC

Config.Name: OIDC Host
Config.Description: Hostname of your identity provider

Config.Name: OIDC Scheme
Config.Description: Protocol (https or http)

Config.Name: OIDC Port
Config.Description: Port number

Config.Name: OIDC Authorization Endpoint
Config.Description: Authorization endpoint path

Config.Name: OIDC Token Endpoint
Config.Description: Token endpoint path

Config.Name: OIDC Userinfo Endpoint
Config.Description: User info endpoint path

Config.Name: SMTP Server
Config.Description: Your SMTP server hostname

Config.Name: SMTP Port
Config.Description: Your SMTP port (typically 587 for TLS)

Config.Name: SMTP Domain
Config.Description: HELO/EHLO domain. For transactional relays (Brevo, Mailgun, SendGrid, Postmark, Resend), set this to your verified sender domain - typically the part after @ in SMTP_FROM.

Config.Name: SMTP Username
Config.Description: Your SMTP username

Config.Name: SMTP Password
Config.Description: Your SMTP password

Config.Name: SMTP From
Config.Description: Email address to send emails from

Config.Name: SMTP Authentication
Config.Description: Auth mechanism. Common values: plain, login (Office 365 / Microsoft 365 requires this), and cram_md5. Use none for an unauthenticated relay. digest_md5, gssapi, ntlm, and xoauth2 are also accepted but rarely useful.

Config.Name: SMTP StartTLS
Config.Description: Opportunistic TLS upgrade on port 587. Leave true for internet-facing relays. Set false only for plain SMTP on port 25 to a trusted local relay. No effect on port 465 (SMTPS / implicit TLS).

Config.Name: SMTP Open Timeout
Config.Description: Seconds to wait for the TCP connection. Bump to 25 for slow providers.

Config.Name: SMTP Read Timeout
Config.Description: Seconds to wait for an SMTP response. Bump to 25 for slow providers.
